full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus the present petitioners as pre-emptors tiled a pre-emption Miscellaneous Case in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, Barisal being Miscellaneous Case No. 09 of 2000 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, contending inter alia that the case land originally belonged to one Tulshi Lal Banik.  The opposite party No.1 was a monthly tenant\under the pre-emptors and other co-sharers of the case land. On 15.03.2000 A.D. the pre-emptors while demanded arrear of rent of the premises the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 disclosed that he has purchased 4 annas share of the land from the opposite party No.2. Thereafter, having obtained the certified copy of the kabla deed the pre-emptors finally came to learn that the vendor-opposite party no.2 transferred the case land in favour of the opposite party no.1 by a registered sub-kabla deed dated 19.01.1999 A.D. The kabla deed was registered on 28.12.1999 A.D. The petitioners being co-sharers of the land of S.A. khatian No. 20 are entitled to pre-empt the case land which is urgently required by them and as a result for getting the land pre-empted the pre-emptor-appellant-petitioners instituted the original miscellaneous case. 

 3. Vis-a-vis; the contrary case of the contesting opposite party Nos. 1(ka)-1(Cha) in short is thus that the case is barred by limitation and the case holding relating to the land of case kabla having been separated on an application filed, from the side of the pre-emptors' father the pre-emptors are seized to be the co-sharers of the case land and as such they are not entitled to pre-empt the case land. The further case of the opposite parties is such that the pre-emptor's father opened different khatians by mutation cases and paid rent separately during his life time and that's why the pre-emptors had no locustandi. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner's submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court committed illegality in dismissing the original case and its subsequent appeal. Only for one reason the pre-emption miscellaneous case was dismissed, which is 'separation of jama'. The original S.A. khatian no. 20 corresponding to the case land has been separated on 22.09.1991, but no court considered that the mutation case by dint of which the 'jama' was separated has been set aside subsequently in Miscellaneous case No. 29 K.T./99-2000 vide exhibit-`ga'. The learned Advocate further submits that the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Barisal has been submitted before the learned appellate court for taking notice as additional evidence but the appellate court without considering the papers passed the impugned judgment and order illegally. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the order dated 29.03.2000 passed by the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land), Barisal in Miscellaneous Case No. 25 K.T./1999-2000 canceling the Sub-division khatian Nos. 554 and 698 was considered by the learned appellate court and from the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Barisal it is apparent that the Sub-division khatian No. 554 and 698 have no existence and the original holding of the S.A. khatian No. 20 remained intact and the pre-emptors as such remained co-sharers to the original holding. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners the teamed Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the submissions advanced from the side of the pre-emptor-petitioners and submits that it is the concurrent findings of both the courts below that the pre-emptor-petitioners are seized to be the co-sharers of the case land which was transferred in favour of the pre-emptee-opposite parties. The case kabla was registered on 28.12.1999 under section 60 of the Registration Act and the case holding was separated on 21.09.1991 at the instance of the father of the pre-emptors namely Narayon Chandra Banik. The vendor of the case land separated the juma in his name on 03.08.1999 and thereafter executed the case kabla in favour of the vendee. Admittedly; the original S.A. khatian is 20 and the mutation khatian is 554. This mutation khatian no 554 stands recorded in the name of the pre-emptor-petitioner's father vide exhibit-kha. Within the content of the case kabla (exhibit-ka) there is a recital that the father of the pre-emptors and the vendor of the ease kabla opened separate khatians. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court not considered the subsequent cancellation of the mutation case as alleged from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioners is not correct. The correct proposition is such that both the courts below considering the facts and circumstances of the case held that the act of cancellation is mulafide which is 'after thought' for the very purpose of the pre-emption miscellaneous case. The learned Advocate also submits that the exhibited documents especially; exhibit-`ka' goes to show that after the death of the pre-emptor's father in imitation case No. 432(1K.T.)/1995-96 the petitioners has opened separate khatian pursuant to previous mutation case No. 554. Thereafter, at the instance of one Meghnath Paul an application under section 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was filed on 29.03.2000 for amalgamation of the holding after cancellation of all previous mutation on the ground that no notice was served upon the co-sharers. It further appears that on the same date i.e. on 29.03.2000 without serving notice the order of amalgamation was given by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Barisal. The learned Advocate submits that under sections 116 and 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 service of notice is a pre-condition of the order of amalgamation of holding. But the fact remains that no notice was served upon the co-sharers of the land. In this context; the learned Advocate referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 37 DLR(AD)212. The Advocate lastly submits that both the courts below in their observation and findings concurrently held that the order of amalgamation would not help the pre-emptor-petitioners as because the kabla deed against which the pre-emption miscellaneous ease was instituted is prior to the amalgamation of the holding and with a malice subsequently the order of amalgamation was obtained for the very purpose of the miscellaneous case for getting the land pre-empted. There is no such illegality or irregularity or misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and order can be interfered with. 

 11. Scrutinizing the evidence on record it appears that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Barisal vide his order dated 29.03.2000 passed the order of amalgamation pursuant to a miscellaneous case being No. 25 K.T./1999-2000 and after that the jama of the holding was separated and subsequent to that new khatian was opened. 

 14. During hearing of this revisional application the learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners has drawn my attention on ground No. 1 of the revisional application wherein it is cited that the learned District Judge i.e. the lower appellate court committed error of law in not considering that the sub-division of the holding relating to the original S.A. khatian is no more in existence and as such the teamed lower appellate court committed illegality ignoring that the sub-division khatian Nos. 554 and 698 are not in existence at present and the original holding of the S.A. khatian No. 20 remain intact, In this regard; having gone through the impugned judgment and order I have every reason to differ with the learned Advocate Mr. Quayum inasmuch as the learned lower appellate court consulting the relevant papers and evidence on records agreed with the learned Advocate appearing from the side of the respondents therein that the order of amalgamation will not help the appellants since the execution and registration of the case kabla was completed earlier and at the time of registration of the deed there was no existence of the order of amalgamation. It is the observation and decisions of both the courts below that the holding stands separated under the law. It is a fact that the separation of tenancy/jama khatian disentitles the pre-emptors from the right of pre-emption as the status of co-sharership in a tenancy of non-agricultural and ceases through two different ways: One is partition of land and the other is separation of the tenancy by splitting up the jama khatian; as the instant case be. Here in this case the factual aspect is such that, pursuant to mutation case No. 191 K.T./1991- 1992 a new Khatian was opened which is khatian No. 554 in the name of the predecessor-in-interest of the pre-emptor-petitioners vide exhibit-ka'. In order to get an order of pre-emption the petitioners must be co-sharers of the holding and if it is found that at the time of transfer the petitioners are not the co-sharers in the case holding and a new khatian is opened in that case the petitioners cannot be legally entitled to get the pre-emption as sought for.
